_comment: Bob keeps a TO-DO list and it never gets shorter (Bk1 ch2, ch12, ch13, ch21). Ours is the research backlog, rendered the way Guppy reports his: a bracketed count, divided into categories. Add freely; that's the joke.

items.text: Books restored and the cache guarded
items.note: The five ebooks were deleted by a commit-splitting script that ran rm -rf on directories before restoring them from git archive — books/ is gitignored, so nothing came back but .gitkeep. It went unnoticed for hours because .cache/corpus.json survived and every build and test kept passing. Restored from backup 11 Aug 2026. `make corpus` now refuses to overwrite the cache when any book parses to fewer chapters than it already holds, and refuses an empty books/ rather than treating it as an empty corpus; --force overrides. The restored book 1 is the 2016 EPUB rather than the MOBI, which needed a third header detector — see the chapter-parsing notes.

items.text: Browser test harness moved into the repo
items.note: Lived in a scratch directory, so it didn't survive a session and its record-count assertions went stale unnoticed — it asserted 86 records for a whole session after the 87th landed. Now tests/ behind `make test`, run against the shipped dist/index.html rather than the template. Expectations are derived from data/*.json instead of hardcoded. Its first run found two live bugs: build.py's ORDER whitelist was silently dropping `alias` and `priorClaim`, so the HAS LEAD chip matched nothing and Will's "/ Riker" never rendered. Includes a golden-master snapshot of 95 states, so the console restructure can be verified by diff.

items.text: Star chart: three labels still drop, and two judgement calls open
items.note: Gliese 54, Zeta Tucanae and Gliese 877 sit almost on top of each other at the default angle and lose their names to decluttering; rotating separates them. Open questions from the first look: whether the glow is now cut too far, and whether the backdrop at magnitude 6 is too busy behind the systems (5.5 would thin it by 40%). Both are one-line changes.

Everything the Bobs reach fits inside 48.8 ly; the galaxy is ~100,000 ly across, so at that scale the whole story is smaller than a pixel. That's the point of it rather than an obstacle — but any Milky Way rendering is an artist's impression, so it belongs in the decoration bucket, clearly marked. Defer until the local chart is finished.

items.text: Console restructured around a register list
items.note: Every view used to be hardcoded: five tab buttons in the markup, a ternary chain in render(), and state.view special cases in the dossier, the paint step and the resize handler. Adding a sixth register meant editing all of them. Now REGISTERS drives all five, and a new view is one entry plus one render function. Done as a golden-master refactor — the 95-state snapshot was byte-identical before and after, so nothing rendered differently. tests/registers.test.js adds a synthetic register at runtime and checks every hook fires, so the next state.view special case will fail the build rather than rot quietly.

items.text: Chase the 30 dropped-source leads through the text
items.note: Each carries a priorClaim from Taylor's tree or the wiki. The claim isn't drawn, but it says where to look. Anything the books confirm gets promoted; anything they contradict is worth writing up.
Ten POV chapters across books 3 and 4, and no source anywhere names who built him. The last major POV character still unaccounted for.
Jeffrey, Milton and Zeke have a citation for their deaths at 82 Eridani. Nothing names who made them.

A third-generation Hector lost at 82 Eridani and an ~18th-generation Hector emailing Bill in 2343. Either the naming convention broke down or they're two Bobs. Currently two records and the only standing validator warning.
Settled as Bill's clone by the Cast of Characters. The narrative only ever put him on Loki's crew at 82 Eridani, which was suggestive and never stated. Worth a look for a narrative confirmation.

items.text: Light biographical sweep, name by name
items.note: Rebuild born, vessel and designation from the text rather than from the sources we dropped. 17 birth dates, 3 vessels and 43 generation numbers came out in the sweep; some are certainly recoverable by reading around each name.

items.text: Systems: check origin and visited the same way
items.note: Neither field has been verified against the text. Starfleet's location data was purged in-world (Bk4 ch32), so expect real gaps there rather than research failures.

items.text: Confirm books 4 and 5 have no Cast of Characters
items.note: Book 2's appendix rescued ten records and turned up Surly. A quick check of the other volumes' back matter is cheap.

items.text: Second pass on the moot scenes for later generations
items.note: Swept once and declared exhausted, but that was before the parser recovered six chapters. Worth one more pass now the corpus is complete.

Largely derivable from origin, visited and lostAt. Sol, Epsilon Eridani, Delta Eridani, 82 Eridani, Omicron² Eridani, Delta and Gamma Pavonis, Eta Cassiopeiae, Poseidon, Gliese 877, HIP 84051, Alpha Centauri, Ragnarök/Valhalla.

Nine creatures in data/bestiary.json, with its own register and an illustration pipeline. The inherited candidate list was mostly wrong — five of eight entries did not survive checking against the text: landers is Dr. Landers, spits is a human faction, boojums are Quinlan drones, hexghi is the Deltan word for a family group, and snarks are Quinlans, who are people. It also missed dragons entirely, at 191 mentions the most-discussed animal in the series. Still to do: a second pass for Ragnarok and Heaven's River river life, and the 'contested sapience' cases the books deliberately leave open.

Five species and nine polities in data/peoples.json, with its own register. Provenance is graded differently from the tree — species and governments have no parents — so what's recorded is whether the books state a thing or leave it open. Acronyms carry an expansion only where a character expands it on the page: USE is the United States of Eurasia, VEHEMENT keeps Butterworth's own hedge, and FAITH has none because the books never give one. A name may be a people or fauna and never both; validate.py checks the two files against each other. Still to do: the Arcadians and Zjentfen, both single mentions; the human colony governments on Vulcan, Romulus, Poseidon and Newholme; and the Bob factions, which currently live as a field on bobs.json rather than here.
Bill's blog is canon — he needles Bob about not reading it in Bk4 ch5. Site updates belong as dated posts, not changelogs. See the voice guide in CLAUDE.md.
Later. Whatever we do has to survive the no-external-requests rule, so anything visual gets inlined.

Two of nine have art — dragon and kraken, drawn as stroke-only SVG so the console can colour them with currentColor. The rest show a dashed plate with their role mark. Adding one is: draw assets/bestiary/<id>.svg, rebuild. The build refuses art containing a script or an external URL, so the page keeps its promise of zero external requests.

items.text: Second pass on peoples: colonies, minor species, Bob factions
items.note: The register covers the majors. Missing: the human colony governments (Vulcan, Romulus, Poseidon, Newholme, Pangea), the Arcadians and Zjentfen at one mention each, and the question of whether the four Bob factions belong here as polities or stay as a field on bobs.json. They cut across lineage, so they are arguably exactly what a polity is.
